m0039.text:
## Direct answer

Two independent problems compound, and only one of them is Claxedo's.

**The renderer's fault:** the transcript has *no typographic hierarchy above body text*. In the shipped app an `## Heading` and a `**bold phrase**` render pixel-identical, `---` renders as literally nothing, and the loudest visual object on the page is a filename pill. Half the intended typography sits behind a flag the app never sets.

**Not the renderer's fault:** ~90% of the rows you scroll past aren't prose. Measured over the 12 most recent session logs in this project, assistant prose is **1.4% of transcript bytes** and **10.5% of rendered blocks**. That's why it reads badly in Claude too.

---

## A. The render path

`A. SessionContent` (`features/session/ui/content/session-content.tsx:6`) → `A.1 SessionPage` → `A.1.1 MessageTimeline` (`features/session/ui/message-timeline.tsx:216`) → `A.1.1.1 ScrollView[data-slot=session-timeline-scroll]` (`:1775`) → `A.1.1.2 VirtualTimelineRow` (`:1982`) → `A.1.1.3 TimelineRowFrame` (`:1402`, stamps `data-component="session-turn"`) → `A.1.1.4 renderTimelineRow` switch (`:1429`) → `A.1.1.5 Part` (`session-ui/src/components/message-part.tsx:1734`) → `A.1.1.6 Markdown` → `.ui-markdown` (`session-ui/src/components/markdown.css`).

`session-turn.tsx` exists but the app timeline never calls it — its CSS still applies because the selectors are attribute-based.

---

## B. Findings, ranked

### B.1 — The intended typography never ships (root cause of several others)

`data-new-layout` is **read** in two places (`markdown.tsx:548`, `message-part.tsx:501`) and **set** in exactly one: `packages/storybook/.storybook/preview.tsx:51`. Never in app source. I confirmed against the built bundle — `dist-local/assets/index.local-*.js` contains the two readers and no setter. The app therefore always takes the `body:not([data-new-layout])` branch.

Consequences, all live in the product:

- `markdown.css:471-476` collapses **h1–h6 to `--font-size-base` (14px) / `--font-weight-medium` (500) / `--text-strong`**. `strong, b` gets the identical treatment (`:478-480` + base `:76-80`). A heading and a bold span are the same pixels. The only surviving difference between h1/h2/h3 is `margin-top: 28/24/20px` — nobody perceives 4px as a hierarchy level.
- `applyCodeMetadata` (`markdown.tsx:547-552`) *deletes* `data-language` and `data-code-kind` in the app, so the shell-code theming at `markdown.css:180-190` is dead and no code block ever carries a language label.
- `newLayout()` gates message comments, file-part rendering, and a spinner variant (`message-part.tsx:1498, 1570, 2495`) — all permanently off.

### B.2 — Visual weight is inverted relative to meaning

Measured across the same 12 sessions: **3.6 inline-code spans per 100 words** (557 spans / ~15.4k words), plus 147 bold spans in 618 lines. Roughly one code pill every 28 words.

Inline code (`markdown.css:352-366`) receives **five simultaneous treatments**: mono family, `font-weight: medium`, `padding: 1px 0.3rem`, `border-radius`, an `inset 0 0 0 0.5px` ring, and an 8% color-mix background. Bold receives +100 weight units on a UI font at 14px — near the perceptual floor. Headings receive nothing (B.1).

So the strongest accent in the prose is spent on the least semantically important token, and the two things that actually carry structure are the quietest. That single inversion is most of the "ugly."

Two supporting defects:
- Inline code inherits `font-size: var(--font-size-base)` = **14px mono**, while `.shiki` code blocks are `--font-size-compact` = **13px** (`markdown.css:174`). Inline code is *larger* than block code, and mono at the same nominal size as SF Pro looks larger still.
- `--font-size-inline-code: 0.85em` is defined at `ui/src/styles/theme.css:34` and referenced by **nothing** in the repo.

### B.3 — Measure is ~1.5× too long, and grows on bigger screens

`message-timeline.tsx:1415-1420` clamps rows to `md:max-w-192` (48rem/768px), widening to `2xl:max-w-[880px]`, minus `px-5`. That leaves ~728px / ~840px of text at 14px — roughly **100–120 characters per line** against the 45–75 target. (Char count is an estimate from a ~7px average advance; I did not measure in a browser. The clamp values are exact.)

The app already knows the right number: `.ui-user-message-body` (`message-part.css:132-136`) clamps user text to `min(82%, 64ch)`. So one-sentence user messages get a proper 64ch measure, and 3,000-character assistant answers get 120ch. Below a 768px viewport there is no clamp at all.

Widening at `2xl` is backwards — the conventional move is to hold the measure and grow the margins.

### B.4 — Hierarchy is expressed only as vertical gaps, and there are eight of them

`li` 8 · `p` 12 · part gap 12 · table 16 · h3 20 · h2 24 · `pre` 24 · turn gap 24 (`<div class="h-6">`, `message-timeline.tsx:1447`) · h1 28 · `hr` 32.

`hr` is `border: none; height: 0` (`markdown.css:168-172`) — a model-written `---` produces 32px of nothing, indistinguishable from a heading's margin. There is no rule, no background change, no left rail, no turn separator: the entire transcript is one undifferentiated grey column whose only structural signal is a set of gaps that differ by 4px.

List indentation is also non-monotonic: `ul` level 1 = 32px, nested `ul` = 16px (`markdown.css:105-110, 146-152`). Nesting *decreases* the indent step, so depth reads as noise.

### B.5 — The dominant row type is below the legibility floor

Tool rows, work-group summaries (`work-group.css:20, 43`) and the thinking heading (`session-turn.css:56-60`) use `--text-weak` / `--text-weaker`. Computed against `--background-stronger`:

| token | dark (#151515) | light (#fcfcfc) |
|---|---|---|
| `--text-weak` | 4.12:1 | **3.15:1** |
| `--text-weaker` | 2.55:1 | **1.65:1** |

WCAG AA for 14px is 4.5:1. Both fail; light theme fails badly. `work-group.css:16-18` additionally gives a group header the *same* grey as its members by design, so there is no container/content distinction either — everything below the prose is one flat wash of unreadable grey.

### B.6 — Nested scroll traps with invisible scrollbars

Inside the one real scroller (`.ui-session-turn-content`, `session-turn.css:15`) sit fixed-height sub-scrollers: work-group list 224px (`work-group.css:74`), error card 240px (`session-turn.css:75`), message-part 240px ×2 (`:389, :471`), diff view (`:218`). Eleven `scrollbar-width: none` declarations across the transcript CSS, plus `mask-image` edge fades. Content is hidden with no affordance that it exists, and the wheel captures unpredictably.

### B.7 — The body font is a UI font

`--font-family-sans: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, …` (`ui/src/styles/theme.css:2`) resolves to SF Pro Text on macOS, set at 14px / 1.6 with `letter-spacing: normal`. SF Pro is drawn for labels and buttons at short lengths, not long-form reading. A `--letter-spacing-chat: -0.13px` token exists (`theme.css:88`) and markdown never applies it. This is the "generic AI chat" signature and the single biggest lever on whether the surface feels designed.

### B.8 — Minor: two undefined tokens

`--v2-text-text-weak` and `--v2-background-bg-hover` are used in `session-ui` CSS but defined nowhere. The former (`markdown.css:521`, broken-image placeholder) has **no fallback**, so `color` computes to `unset` → inherits full-strength body colour instead of muted.

---

## C. Why it's also ugly in Claude — the content half

Measured over the 12 most recent `.jsonl` transcripts for this project:

**By bytes:** `tool_result` 34.5% · `thinking` 24.7% · images 17.4% · `tool_use` 15.9% · user text 6.1% · **assistant prose 1.4%**

**By block count:** 1,338 `tool_use` · 869 `thinking` · 273 assistant text · 116 user text → ~52% of rows are tool calls, ~33% thinking, **~10.5% prose**.

Nine of every ten rows you scroll past are machine bookkeeping. No renderer fixes that ratio; the fix is editorial — fold the machinery by default and promote the answer. `WorkGroup` (`message-part.tsx:1375`) already does half of this for bash/edit/write runs; it just isn't the default posture for the whole transcript.

The prose shape doesn't help either: **20% of prose lines are list items**, median 22 words per line, only 3% headings. Under a heading system that renders headings as body text (B.1), bullet-heavy prose collapses into a flat pile of similar-looking short lines.

---

## D. Where I'd change it, ranked by effect ÷ effort

1. **Delete the `data-new-layout` fork.** Pick one branch and make it the only one. Everything in B.1 disappears, and ~17 dead CSS blocks plus a dead `newLayout()` gate go with it. This is the canonical-owner fix, not a new feature.
2. **Restore heading scale** — even 20/17/15px at weight 600 against 14px body would give the transcript a spine.
3. **Demote the inline-code pill** to `0.85em` + tint, drop the ring and the medium weight; **promote bold** to 600. Ten minutes, and it fixes the inversion in B.2 that makes prose read as confetti.
4. **Clamp the measure to ~68ch** and stop widening at `2xl`; grow margins instead.
5. **Raise `--text-weak`** to clear 4.5:1 in both themes, and give work-group headers a distinct step from their members.
6. **Make `hr` visible** and give turn boundaries a real separator instead of a 24px hole.
7. **Replace the UI font** for prose with an actual reading face (the transcript is the product; a licensed text face here is the highest-leverage single change in the whole list).

Downside worth naming: (1) is a real migration — the `body[data-new-layout]` branches were written against v2 tokens and have never been exercised in the app, so turning them on will surface a second wave of visual defects rather than fewer. It's still the right direction, because the current state means every transcript style is authored twice and shipped once.

**What I did not verify:** I read this from source and measured it from the session logs. I did not render or screenshot the app, so the characters-per-line figure is an estimate; contrast ratios, token values, spacing values, and the content-composition percentages are computed and exact.

input.prompt:
Repo: /Users/yashvardhansingh/test/opencode (branch feat/terminal-agents-and-dialog-containment). Package: packages/session-ui.

GOAL: convert REAL Claude Code session logs into a checked-in Storybook fixture that the session-ui transcript renderer can consume unchanged. You own exactly two new files. Do not touch anything else — another agent is editing packages/session-ui/src/components/transcript-lab.stories.tsx concurrently, so DO NOT create or edit that file.

## Files you own (create these, nothing else)
1. `packages/session-ui/script/build-transcript-lab-fixture.mjs` — the generator (Node ESM, run with `bun run`).
2. `packages/session-ui/src/components/transcript-lab-fixture.ts` — its generated, checked-in output.

Also add ONE line to `packages/session-ui/package.json` scripts:
`"build:transcript-lab-fixture": "bun run script/build-transcript-lab-fixture.mjs"`

## Input data
Real logs live at `/Users/yashvardhansingh/.claude/projects/-Users-yashvardhansingh-test-opencode/*.jsonl` (Claude Code transcript format, one JSON object per line).

Generate the fixture from TWO sessions so the lab can switch between them:
- `e8fbc92a-aef1-4e76-b08c-55ec4212eac5.jsonl` — prose-heavy; key id `"diagnosis"`, title `"Transcript readability diagnosis"`.
- Pick ONE more from the 5 most recently modified that is tool-heavy (many tool_use blocks, little prose); key id `"toolrun"`, title = a short human title you derive from its first user message.

## Output contract — read these files FIRST, do not guess
- `packages/agent-runtime-contract/src/content.ts` — the exact types: `AgentUserMessage`, `AgentAssistantMessage`, `AgentPresentationMessage`, `AgentContentPart`, `AgentTextPart`, `AgentReasoningPart`, `AgentToolPart`, `AgentToolState`.
- `packages/session-ui/src/context/data.tsx` — the `Data` store shape the `DataProvider` takes (`session`, `session_status`, `session_diff`, `message`, `part`).
- `packages/session-ui/src/components/session-turn.tsx:182-290` — how `SessionTurn` selects a turn: it finds the user message by `props.messageID`, then collects every assistant message where `parentID === userMessage.id`, and reads parts from `data.store.part[message.id]`.
- `packages/session-ui/src/components/message-part.tsx` `getToolInfo(tool, input, metadata)` — the tool-name switch. Your `AgentToolPart.tool` values MUST be names this switch actually handles (they are lowercase, e.g. `read`, `bash`, `edit`, `write`, `grep`, `glob`, `list`, `todowrite`, `webfetch`, `task`). Read the switch and write an explicit mapping table from Claude Code's PascalCase tool names to it. Anything unmapped: lowercase it and let the default branch handle it.

`transcript-lab-fixture.ts` must export:
```ts
export type TranscriptLabSession = {
  id: string
  title: string
  sessionID: string
  /** Ordered; user messages first in their turn. Sorted by `id` for Binary.search. */
  messages: AgentPresentationMessage[]
  /** Keyed by messageID, matching Data["part"]. */
  parts: Record<string, AgentContentPart[]>
  /** Measured from the source log, for the lab's stats strip. */
  stats: { userTurns: number; assistantMessages: number; textParts: number; reasoningParts: number; toolParts: number; proseChars: number; machineryChars: number }
}
export const TRANSCRIPT_LAB_SESSIONS: TranscriptLabSession[]
```
Import the types with `import type { ... } from "@claxedo/agent-runtime-contract"`. The file must typecheck under `bun run typecheck` in packages/session-ui with NO `@ts-nocheck` and NO `as any`.

## Conversion rules
- A jsonl row with `message.role === "user"` whose content is a string, or an array containing a `text` block, becomes an `AgentUserMessage`. Its text becomes a single `AgentTextPart` in `parts[messageID]`.
- A row with `message.role === "user"` whose content array holds only `tool_result` blocks is NOT a user message — fold each `tool_result` into the matching earlier `tool_use` part (match on `tool_use_id` === the tool part's `callID`).
- `message.role === "assistant"` rows become `AgentAssistantMessage`, with `parentID` set to the id of the most recent user message. Content blocks map to parts, in order: `text` → `AgentTextPart`; `thinking` → `AgentReasoningPart` (its `text` is the `thinking` field); `tool_use` → `AgentToolPart` with `callID` = block `id`, `tool` = mapped name, `state.input` = block `input`.
- Tool state: `{ status: "completed", input, output, title, metadata: {}, time: { start, end } }` where `output` is the tool_result content flattened to a string. If the tool_result has `is_error: true`, emit `{ status: "error", input, error: <text>, metadata: {}, time: { start, end } }` instead. A tool_use with no matching result stays `{ status: "pending", input, raw: "" }`. Give `title` a short human string (e.g. the file path or command) — mirror what the real app shows if `getToolInfo` reveals it.
- SKIP entirely: rows with `isSidechain: true`, rows with `isMeta: true`, `image` content blocks (they are megabytes of base64 — count how many you dropped and print it), and rows that are not user/assistant messages.
- TRUNCATE each tool `output`/`error` to 8000 characters, appending `"\n… [truncated for fixture]"` when cut. Nothing else gets truncated — prose, thinking and tool inputs stay whole.
- IDs: emit your own zero-padded, lexicographically sortable ids (`m0001`, `m0002`, … and `p0001`, …) and keep `messages` sorted by `id`. `SessionTurn` runs `Binary.search` over `m.id`, so sort order is load-bearing.
- Required fields you must fill plausibly from the log (never invent a field that isn't in the type): `time.created` / `time.completed` from row timestamps; `sessionID`; assistant `cost: 0`, `tokens` from the row's usage if present else zeros, `path: { cwd, root }` from the log's `cwd`, `mode`/`agent`, `modelID`/`providerID` from the row's model.

## Generator ergonomics
`build-transcript-lab-fixture.mjs` takes the log paths as argv (defaulting to the two above), prints a per-session summary to stderr (rows read, rows skipped and why, images dropped, tool results matched/unmatched, final byte size), and writes the .ts file with `prettier`-compatible formatting — check `packages/session-ui` for an oxlint/prettier config and match the repo's style (no semicolons, double quotes, 2-space indent, 120 col — verify against a neighbouring .ts file rather than trusting me).

The generated file must start with a comment naming the exact command to regenerate it, because a reader cannot otherwise know it is generated. That is the ONLY comment the file needs — the repo's CLAUDE.md bans restating what code already says.

## Acceptance — actually run these and report the real output
1. `cd packages/session-ui && bun run build:transcript-lab-fixture` → succeeds, prints the summary.
2. `cd packages/session-ui && bun run typecheck` → report the exact result. If there are pre-existing errors unrelated to your file, say so and list only yours.
3. Report the final size of `transcript-lab-fixture.ts` in KB and the `stats` object for each session.
4. Sanity-assert in your report: for each session, every `AgentAssistantMessage.parentID` resolves to a user message that exists in `messages`, and every `parts` key is a message id that exists. State how you checked.

Keep the fixture under ~1.5 MB total. If it exceeds that, reduce the number of turns kept (take the FIRST N complete turns, never sample randomly) and say exactly what you dropped. Report the file paths you wrote and nothing else you changed.

input.message:
Format change needed on your output file, with evidence. Please emit the fixture as JSON data plus a thin typed wrapper, instead of one big `.ts`.

The fixture embeds real transcript text, and that text contains source code — including, self-referentially, the transcript lab's own CSS and my agent prompts. Two repo guards scan `.ts`/`.tsx` under `packages/session-ui/src` as *source* and match inside those string literals:

1. `packages/session-ui$ bun test src/components/markdown-svg-sanitize.test.ts` → `no unsanitized markup sinks > every innerHTML assignment is a known-sanitized value` fails, reporting `transcript-lab-fixture.ts: .innerHTML = ...`. The guard regex is `/\.innerHTML\s*=\s*([^\n]+?)\s*$/gm` over raw file text (test lines 212-237); it cannot tell an assignment from a quoted one.
2. `packages/claxedo-app$ bun run lint:theme-tokens` exits 1. I checked all of it — **every finding is in `transcript-lab-fixture.ts`**, zero in any real source file. Because that script is the FIRST step of `claxedo-app`'s `typecheck` chain (`lint:theme-tokens && test:architecture && tsgo -b && …`), the fixture currently blocks that whole package's typecheck.

Both are false positives, and both will recur unpredictably with any regenerated transcript — the next session that discusses `innerHTML` or a hex colour re-breaks them. Exempting the guards would be shaping the tests around the result, and would blunt guards that exist for good reasons. The root cause is that generated *data* is sitting in the source tree wearing a source extension.

So please restructure to:

- `packages/session-ui/src/components/transcript-lab-fixture.json` — the generated data. Neither guard scans `.json`.
- `packages/session-ui/src/components/transcript-lab-fixture.ts` — hand-written, short, checked in, containing only: the `TranscriptLabSession` type, the JSON import, and a single documented cast at that boundary. No transcript text. It must stay small enough that a reader can see at a glance that it holds no markup sink and no design values.

Keep the public API identical — `TRANSCRIPT_LAB_SESSIONS` and `TranscriptLabSession` exported from `./transcript-lab-fixture` — because my story imports exactly that and I do not want to change it.

Watch out for two things:
- If `resolveJsonModule` makes tsgo infer a huge literal type from a ~1 MB JSON and slows or blows up the typecheck, prefer declaring the module's shape (a `.d.ts` or an explicit annotation on the import) over letting inference walk the whole file. Measure `bun run typecheck` before and after and report both timings.
- Confirm the JSON import actually resolves in the Storybook Vite build, not just in tsgo. The story is at `packages/session-ui/src/components/transcript-lab.stories.tsx`; Storybook runs from `packages/storybook` (`bun run storybook`, port 6006, currently up).

Acceptance, please run and report real output for all four:
1. `packages/session-ui$ bun run build:transcript-lab-fixture`
2. `packages/session-ui$ bun test src/components/markdown-svg-sanitize.test.ts` → expect 23 pass, 0 fail
3. `packages/claxedo-app$ bun run lint:theme-tokens` → expect exit 0, or if findings remain, list them and confirm none are in your files
4. `packages/session-ui$ bun run typecheck`

This supersedes nothing else in your brief — the catalog session and the reasoning-text work still stand.

Both are real defects, not one. I traced the flow and confirmed the grouping half by running the actual function.

## A. Clicking a skill does nothing — a bug

`A.1 ToolPartDisplay` (`packages/session-ui/src/components/message-part.tsx:1853`) resolves a renderer via `ToolRegistry.render(part().tool)` → `A.1.1` the `skill` renderer at `message-part.tsx:3150`:

```tsx
return <BasicTool icon="brain" status={props.status} trigger={trigger()} hideDetails />
```

Compare it to every other renderer (`read`, `bash`, `grep` at `:2292`), which do `<BasicTool {...props} …>{output}</BasicTool>`. The skill one:

1. Hardcodes `hideDetails`, which in `basic-tool.tsx:323` gates away `Collapsible.Content` entirely.
2. Never spreads `{...props}` and never forwards `props.output` — so `hasChildren()` (`basic-tool.tsx:108`) is false and `basic-tool.tsx:292` suppresses the chevron. The skill's output is discarded; the storybook fixture at `timeline-playground.stories.tsx:437` even supplies `output: "Skill loaded successfully"` that the renderer throws away.
3. Passes no `onTriggerClick` / `triggerHref` / `clickable`. `webfetch` (`:2337`) and `task` (`:2521`) are also `hideDetails` but attach navigation instead.

The row is still wrapped in a Kobalte `Collapsible.Trigger` — a real `<button>`, focusable, with a hover brighten (`basic-tool.css:390`) and a focus background (`collapsible.css:57`). So it *looks* interactive, and your click does reach `handleOpenChange` and flips `state.open` — it just opens an empty region. A dead toggle, not a missing handler.

Side effect of the same omission: skills also drop `startedAt` (no live "for Xs"), `defaultOpen`, and the timeline's controlled `open`/`onOpenChange`, so `groupOpen` persistence in `message-timeline.tsx:677` is ignored for them.

## B. Commands not grouped — also a bug, on the Claude harness

Grouping lives in `groupParts()` (`message-timeline.data.ts:537`) and matches against **lowercase-only** sets:

```ts
const contextGroupTools = new Set(["read", "glob", "grep", "list", "read_file"])
const workGroupTools = new Set(["bash", "command", "shell", …])
const hiddenTools = new Set(["todowrite"])
```

But `packages/agent-event-runtime/src/harnesses/claude/adapter.ts:249` copies the SDK's tool name **verbatim**, and the native Claude SDK capitalizes: `Bash`, `Read`, `Skill`, `Task`. The recorded fixture confirms it — `e2e/fixtures/harness-traces/claude-sdk.json` contains exactly one tool, `"Grep"`, while `opencode.json` has `bash`/`read`/`skill` lowercase.

The renderer registry survives this because `getTool` lowercases (`message-part.tsx:1794`). The grouping pass does not. I ran the real `Timeline.constructMessageRows` to confirm:

```
lowercase bash x3        -> [ "work" ]          ← one accordion
lowercase read x3        -> [ "context" ]
CAPITAL  Bash x3         -> [ "part", "part", "part" ]   ← three loud rows
CAPITAL  Read x3         -> [ "part", "part", "part" ]
bash,bash,skill,bash,bash-> [ "work", "part", "work" ]   ← skill splits the run
```

Two findings there. Capitalized names never group at all. And `skill` isn't in any group set even lowercase, so it *flushes* an in-progress run and splits one work accordion into two. (Any interleaved assistant text does the same.) `isSubagentToolPart` (`subagent-presentation.ts:51`) is case-sensitive too, so `Task` never becomes a subagent chip.

## C. The "Working" toggle — this part *is* intentional

`TurnFoldRow` (`message-timeline-turn-rows.tsx:42`) renders "Working for Xs" / "Worked for Xs". It's driven by `message-timeline.data.ts:203`:

```ts
const canFoldRunning = running && foldWhileRunning && foldableCount >= 3
```

`foldWhileRunning` comes from `settings.general.timelineFoldWhileRunning()`, which **defaults to `true`** (`platform/settings/provider.tsx:120`) and has no settings-UI control and no i18n label anywhere — it's a hidden setting you can only change by editing the store. By design it keeps the last live group visible; but since B turns every tool into its own foldable "part", the threshold of 3 trips almost immediately and there's much more behind the fold than intended.

So: the fold itself is expected. Needing two clicks (fold → work accordion, which also defaults closed at `message-timeline.tsx:1324`, `groupOpen[key] ?? false`) is the compounding effect of B.

One more thing worth knowing: the e2e test at `core-harness-rendering-matrix.spec.ts:753` is named *"raw \"Grep\" falls back to GenericTool"*, but `ui.tool.grep` is literally `"Grep"` (`packages/ui/src/i18n/en.ts:136`), so its assertion passes identically whether the real grep renderer or `GenericTool` rendered. It doesn't prove its own claim — which is presumably how the case mismatch stayed invisible.

Want me to fix these? The three are independent: (1) give `skill` a real body or a real click target, (2) lowercase the tool name at the harness adapter boundary so *all* consumers agree, (3) decide whether `skill` should join a group set or stay a standalone marker.

Status: observations only. Nothing here has been changed. Each entry names the
canonical owner, the evidence, and whether the behavior is a defect or an
intentional design that a defect makes worse.

Reported by the user on 2026-09-09 while driving a live session.

## Verification method

Findings marked **measured** were produced by calling the real
`Timeline.constructMessageRows` from `message-timeline.data.ts` in a temporary
`bun:test` probe (since removed) and printing the resulting row tags. Findings
marked **read** come from reading the implementation only.

---

## D1 — The `skill` tool row is a dead click target

Owner: `packages/session-ui/src/components/message-part.tsx:3150` (the `skill`
entry in `ToolRegistry`).

```tsx
return <BasicTool icon="brain" status={props.status} trigger={trigger()} hideDetails />
```

Every other renderer (`read` :2196, `grep` :2292, `bash` :2558) does
`<BasicTool {...props} …>{output}</BasicTool>`. The `skill` one differs three ways:

1. `hideDetails` is hardcoded, and `basic-tool.tsx:323` gates `Collapsible.Content`
   on `hasChildren() && !props.hideDetails`.
2. No `{...props}` spread and no `props.output`, so `hasChildren()`
   (`basic-tool.tsx:108`) is false. `basic-tool.tsx:292` therefore also suppresses
   the chevron. The skill's output is discarded — the storybook fixture at
   `timeline-playground.stories.tsx:437` supplies `output: "Skill loaded successfully"`
   that never renders.
3. No `onTriggerClick` / `triggerHref` / `clickable`. `webfetch` (:2337) and `task`
   (:2521) are also `hideDetails` but attach navigation instead.

The row is still a Kobalte `Collapsible.Trigger` — a real `<button>`, focusable,
with a hover brighten (`basic-tool.css:390`) and focus background
(`collapsible.css:57`). A click reaches `handleOpenChange` (`basic-tool.tsx:211`)
and flips `state.open` onto nothing. It is a dead toggle, not a missing handler.

Collateral from the same omission: `startedAt` (no live elapsed), `defaultOpen`,
and the timeline's controlled `open`/`onOpenChange` are all dropped, so the
per-part open persistence in `message-timeline.tsx:677` is ignored for skills.

Read.

## D2 — Claude-harness tool names never group (case mismatch)

Owner: the lowercase-only sets in
`packages/claxedo-app/src/features/session/ui/message-timeline.data.ts:458-470`.

```ts
const contextGroupTools = new Set(["read", "glob", "grep", "list", "read_file"])
const workGroupTools    = new Set(["bash", "command", "shell", …])
const hiddenTools       = new Set(["todowrite"])
```

`packages/agent-event-runtime/src/harnesses/claude/adapter.ts:249` copies the SDK
tool name verbatim, and the native Claude SDK capitalizes: `Bash`, `Read`, `Skill`,
`Task`. The recorded fixture confirms it — `e2e/fixtures/harness-traces/claude-sdk.json`
contains exactly one tool name, `"Grep"`, where `opencode.json` has `bash`/`read`/`skill`.

The renderer registry survives because `getTool` lowercases
(`message-part.tsx:1794`). The grouping pass does not, and neither does
`isSubagentToolPart` (`subagent-presentation.ts:51`, `part.tool === "task"`), so
`Task` never becomes a subagent chip either.

Measured, via `constructMessageRows`:

```
lowercase bash x3         -> [ "work" ]                     one accordion
lowercase read x3         -> [ "context" ]
CAPITAL  Bash x3          -> [ "part", "part", "part" ]     three loud rows
CAPITAL  Read x3          -> [ "part", "part", "part" ]
CAPITAL  Bash,Read,Skill,Task -> [ "part", "part", "part", "part" ]
```

Fix direction: normalize once at the harness adapter boundary so every consumer
agrees, rather than adding capitalized aliases to each set.

## D3 — `skill` splits a work run in two

Owner: `groupParts` in `message-timeline.data.ts:537`.

`skill` is in no group set, so it falls to the final branch (`:622-625`) which
flushes the in-progress context/work/task runs before emitting itself. Measured:

```
bash,bash,skill,bash,bash -> [ "work", "part", "work" ]
```

Interleaved assistant text does the same. On a harness that emits many short
prose fragments between tool calls this is a large share of the "commands are
not grouped" symptom, independent of D2.

## D4 — The auto-fold swallows subagent cards

Owner: `isGroupFoldable` and `canFoldSettled` in `message-timeline.data.ts:171-200`.

The comment at `:196-199` states the intent:

> A single tool is already one compact, useful row. Folding it replaces the only
> actionable content with an extra click and breaks the established
> standalone-tool/task-card contract.

But the guard is only `foldableCount >= 2`, and `isGroupFoldable` returns true for
the `agents` group type and for any standalone tool part — including a `task`. So
the task-card contract that comment protects holds only for a turn whose *entire*
tool activity is subagents. Measured:

```
2 tasks + 1 bash -> [ UserMessage, TurnFold(folded=true, count=2) ]
1 task  + 2 bash -> [ UserMessage, TurnFold(folded=true, count=2) ]
1 task  + 1 bash -> [ UserMessage, TurnFold(folded=true, count=2) ]
3 tasks only     -> [ UserMessage, AssistantPart(agents) ]      survives
1 task only      -> [ UserMessage, AssistantPart(part) ]        survives
```

The rule is inverted from the intent: the more real work a turn does alongside a
subagent, the more certain the subagent card is to disappear behind
"Worked for Xs". D2 makes this near-universal on the Claude harness, because every
capitalized tool becomes its own foldable `part` and `foldableCount` passes 2 immediately.

## D5 — `timelineFoldWhileRunning` is on by default with no way to turn it off

Owner: `packages/claxedo-app/src/platform/settings/provider.tsx:120`.

`timelineFoldWhileRunning` defaults to `true` and is consumed at
`message-timeline.tsx:570` → `canFoldRunning` (`message-timeline.data.ts:203`).
There is no settings-UI control and no i18n label for it anywhere in the repo, so
it can only be changed by editing the settings store by hand.

The fold itself is intentional design and keeps the last live group visible. It is
listed here because D2 and D4 push far more behind it than the design assumed, and
because a user who dislikes it has no supported way to opt out.

## D6 — `core-harness-rendering-matrix.spec.ts:753` does not test what it claims

The test is named *"raw \"Grep\" falls back to GenericTool"* and asserts a
`basic-tool-tool-title` with text `"Grep"`. But `ui.tool.grep` is literally
`"Grep"` (`packages/ui/src/i18n/en.ts:136`), and `getTool` lowercases, so the real
`grep` renderer produces the same title. The assertion passes under either
renderer and cannot distinguish them. This is presumably how D2 stayed invisible.

Reported. Investigation pending.

## D8 — Subagent card overflows the transcript column width

Reported. Investigation pending.

Reported. Investigation pending.

cat > docs/plans/2026-09-09-003-session-transcript-defect-log.md <<'MDEOF'
# Session transcript, composer, and navigation defect log

Status: observations only. Nothing here has been changed.

Reported by the user on 2026-09-09 while driving a live session. Each entry names
the canonical owner, the evidence, and whether the behavior is a defect or an
intentional design that a defect makes worse.

## Verification method

Findings marked **measured** were produced by calling the real
`Timeline.constructMessageRows` from `message-timeline.data.ts` in a temporary
`bun:test` probe (since removed) and printing the resulting row tags. Findings
marked **read** come from reading the implementation only.

## Standing requirement (user, 2026-09-09)

> No matter what happens there should be no content shift when I jump from one
> session to another.

This governs D11 and constrains any fix to D4/D5: switching sessions must not
reorder, reflow, or re-fold anything under the pointer.

---

## D1 — The `skill` tool row is a dead click target

Owner: `packages/session-ui/src/components/message-part.tsx:3150`.

```tsx
return <BasicTool icon="brain" status={props.status} trigger={trigger()} hideDetails />
```

Every other renderer (`read` :2196, `grep` :2292, `bash` :2558) does
`<BasicTool {...props} …>{output}</BasicTool>`. This one differs three ways:

1. `hideDetails` is hardcoded; `basic-tool.tsx:323` gates `Collapsible.Content` on
   `hasChildren() && !props.hideDetails`.
2. No `{...props}` spread and no `props.output`, so `hasChildren()`
   (`basic-tool.tsx:108`) is false and `basic-tool.tsx:292` also suppresses the
   chevron. The skill's output is discarded — the storybook fixture at
   `timeline-playground.stories.tsx:437` supplies
   `output: "Skill loaded successfully"` that never renders.
3. No `onTriggerClick` / `triggerHref` / `clickable`. `webfetch` (:2337) and `task`
   (:2521) are also `hideDetails` but attach navigation instead.

The row is still a Kobalte `Collapsible.Trigger` — a real `<button>`, focusable,
with a hover brighten (`basic-tool.css:390`) and focus background
(`collapsible.css:57`). A click reaches `handleOpenChange` (`basic-tool.tsx:211`)
and flips `state.open` onto nothing. A dead toggle, not a missing handler.

Collateral: `startedAt` (no live elapsed), `defaultOpen`, and the timeline's
controlled `open`/`onOpenChange` are dropped, so per-part open persistence
(`message-timeline.tsx:677`) is ignored for skills.

Read.

## D2 — Claude-harness tool names never group (case mismatch)

Owner: the lowercase-only sets in `message-timeline.data.ts:458-470`.

```ts
const contextGroupTools = new Set(["read", "glob", "grep", "list", "read_file"])
const workGroupTools    = new Set(["bash", "command", "shell", …])
const hiddenTools       = new Set(["todowrite"])
```

`packages/agent-event-runtime/src/harnesses/claude/adapter.ts:249` copies the SDK
tool name verbatim, and the native Claude SDK capitalizes: `Bash`, `Read`,
`Skill`, `Task`. The fixture confirms it — `e2e/fixtures/harness-traces/claude-sdk.json`
contains exactly one tool name, `"Grep"`, where `opencode.json` has
`bash`/`read`/`skill`.

The renderer registry survives because `getTool` lowercases
(`message-part.tsx:1794`). The grouping pass does not, and neither does
`isSubagentToolPart` (`subagent-presentation.ts:51`, `part.tool === "task"`), so
`Task` never becomes a subagent chip either.

Measured:

```
lowercase bash x3             -> [ "work" ]                       one accordion
lowercase read x3             -> [ "context" ]
CAPITAL  Bash x3              -> [ "part", "part", "part" ]       three loud rows
CAPITAL  Read x3              -> [ "part", "part", "part" ]
CAPITAL  Bash,Read,Skill,Task -> [ "part", "part", "part", "part" ]
```

Fix direction: normalize once at the harness adapter boundary so every consumer
agrees, rather than adding capitalized aliases to each set.

## D3 — `skill` splits a work run in two

Owner: `groupParts`, `message-timeline.data.ts:537`.

`skill` is in no group set, so it falls to the final branch (:622-625), which
flushes the in-progress context/work/task runs before emitting itself. Measured:

```
bash,bash,skill,bash,bash -> [ "work", "part", "work" ]
```

Interleaved assistant text does the same. On a harness that emits short prose
between tool calls this is a large share of the "commands are not grouped"
symptom, independent of D2.

## D4 — The auto-fold swallows subagent cards

Owner: `isGroupFoldable` / `canFoldSettled`, `message-timeline.data.ts:171-200`.

The comment at :196-199 states the intent:

> A single tool is already one compact, useful row. Folding it replaces the only
> actionable content with an extra click and breaks the established
> standalone-tool/task-card contract.

But the guard is only `foldableCount >= 2`, and `isGroupFoldable` returns true for
the `agents` group type and for any standalone tool part — including a `task`. The
task-card contract that comment protects therefore holds only for a turn whose
*entire* tool activity is subagents. Measured:

```
2 tasks + 1 bash -> [ UserMessage, TurnFold(folded=true, count=2) ]
1 task  + 2 bash -> [ UserMessage, TurnFold(folded=true, count=2) ]
1 task  + 1 bash -> [ UserMessage, TurnFold(folded=true, count=2) ]
3 tasks only     -> [ UserMessage, AssistantPart(agents) ]      survives
1 task only      -> [ UserMessage, AssistantPart(part) ]        survives
```

The rule is inverted from the intent: the more real work a turn does alongside a
subagent, the more certain the subagent card is to disappear behind
"Worked for Xs". D2 makes this near-universal on the Claude harness, because every
capitalized tool becomes its own foldable `part` and `foldableCount` passes 2
immediately.

## D5 — `timelineFoldWhileRunning` is on by default with no way to turn it off

Owner: `packages/claxedo-app/src/platform/settings/provider.tsx:120`.

Defaults to `true`; consumed at `message-timeline.tsx:570` → `canFoldRunning`
(`message-timeline.data.ts:203`). There is no settings-UI control and no i18n label
for it anywhere in the repo, so it can only be changed by hand-editing the store.

The fold itself is intentional and keeps the last live group visible. Listed here
because D2 and D4 push far more behind it than the design assumed, and because a
user who dislikes it has no supported way to opt out.

## D6 — `core-harness-rendering-matrix.spec.ts:753` does not test what it claims

Named *"raw \"Grep\" falls back to GenericTool"*, it asserts a
`basic-tool-tool-title` with text `"Grep"`. But `ui.tool.grep` is literally
`"Grep"` (`packages/ui/src/i18n/en.ts:136`) and `getTool` lowercases, so the real
`grep` renderer produces the same title. The assertion passes under either
renderer and cannot distinguish them. Presumably how D2 stayed invisible.

## D7 — Subagent card does not reliably open in the right workspace panel

Owner: `openSubagent`, `packages/claxedo-app/src/features/session/ui/message-timeline.tsx:240`.

The right-hand split is conditional:

```ts
if (window.matchMedia(`(min-width: ${BP_MD}px)`).matches && paneId && !childPane && !dedicatedPane) {
  claxedoState.layout.splitContent(paneId, "right", contentId)
} else if (dedicatedPane && !childPane) {
  claxedoState.wb.panes.assign(dedicatedPane, contentId)
  claxedoState.layout.showContent(contentId)
} else {
  claxedoState.layout.showContent(contentId)
}
```

Four independent conditions must all hold to get a right split. Any one failing
falls through to bare `showContent(contentId)`, which surfaces the subagent in the
*current* pane instead of a right panel. The card is also opened with
`focus: false`, and the post-open focus call targets
`[data-subagent-child-heading]` inside a `requestAnimationFrame`, so it silently
does nothing if that node has not mounted yet.

Read. Not yet narrowed to which of the four conditions fails in the reported case
— needs a live repro with the window width and existing pane layout recorded.

## D8 — Subagent card overflows the transcript column

Reported. Not yet investigated; the two background agents assigned to D7/D8 were
killed before reporting.

## D9 — Videos cannot be attached to the composer (by design, not by filter)

Owner: `attachmentMime`, `packages/claxedo-app/src/features/session/composer/ui/files.ts:52`.

The paste handler itself (`attachments.ts:93`) does **not** filter by MIME — it
accepts any `item.kind === "file"`. The rejection is downstream:

```ts
export async function attachmentMime(file: File) {
  const type = kind(file.type)
  if (IMAGE_MIMES.has(type)) return type
  if (type === "application/pdf") return type
  …
  const bytes = new Uint8Array(await file.slice(0, SAMPLE).arrayBuffer())
  if (!textBytes(bytes)) return undefined     // video lands here
  return "text/plain"
}
```

`IMAGE_MIMES` is `ACCEPTED_IMAGE_TYPES` = `["image/png","image/jpeg","image/gif","image/webp"]`
(`packages/claxedo-app/src/lib/file-picker.ts:1`). A `video/mp4` is not an image,
not a PDF, not text-ish, and sniffs as binary → `undefined` → `add()` shows the
generic "paste unsupported" toast and drops it.

This is deeper than a filter. The attachment the composer builds is hardcoded

`packages/claxedo-app/src/features/session/commands/prompt-admission.ts`.

## D14 — Assistant text can be emitted twice (snapshot/delta reconciliation fallback)

Owner: `packages/agent-event-runtime/src/harnesses/claude/adapter.ts:862-870`.

Assistant text reaches the projection twice over: as streamed `text_delta`s, and
again as a cumulative snapshot on the completed assistant message. The adapter
reconciles them by subtracting what it has already emitted:

```ts
const snapshot = assistantSnapshotText(rawMessage)
const childOwned = !!claudeChildCorrelationKey(rawMessage)
const deltaText = childOwned
  ? snapshot                                             // 1
  : snapshot.startsWith(state.emittedAssistantText)
    ? snapshot.slice(state.emittedAssistantText.length)   // 2  correct: emit the tail
    : state.emittedAssistantText.endsWith(snapshot)
      ? ""                                               // 3  already emitted
      : snapshot                                         // 4  emit EVERYTHING again
```

Branch 4 is a duplication fallback: when the snapshot is neither a continuation of
the emitted text nor already contained in it, the adapter re-emits the **entire
snapshot** on top of the deltas already streamed. The message then renders twice.

Reaching branch 4 requires only that the deltas and the snapshot diverge before
their common tail. The adapter creates that divergence itself — `:763-768` drops
`citations_delta`, `signature_delta`, and `compaction_delta` with the note
*"delta type has no dedicated AgentRuntimeEvent equivalent"*. Content dropped from

snapshot nor a superset of it, which is exactly branch 4.

Branch 1 is a second exposure: for child (subagent) messages the full snapshot is
always emitted, and the state update deliberately skips recording it —
`...(snapshot && !childOwned ? { emittedAssistantText: snapshot } : {})`. Two
snapshots for the same child message therefore emit their full text twice with no
suppression possible.

## D15 — A resolved question flashes when navigating back to a session

Owner: `applyDirectorySessionMeta`,
`packages/claxedo-app/src/features/session/store/directory-session-meta.ts:21`.

The pending permissions/questions the docks read are a pure client cache. The
query is declared with `queryFn: skipToken, enabled: false`
(`store/session-pane-queries.ts:58`), so it never refetches — it holds whatever
was last dispatched into it, keyed by session id, and keeps holding it after you
navigate away.

Answering a question clears that entry by dispatching a fresh `session.requests`
(`ui/composer/session-question-dock.tsx:213`). Returning to the session re-runs
the directory status/permission/question hydration, which calls
`applyDirectorySessionMeta` and dispatches `session.requests` again from that
read. If that read was taken or cached before the answer landed, it re-seeds the
already-answered question into the cache; the next authoritative event clears it
again. The dock renders in between — the brief flash.

Two writers with no ordering guarantee feed one cache entry. The module's own
header comment already names this hazard for status:

> This payload has two independent authorities that fetch it — the session pane's
> hydration (`syncSessionMeta`) and the rail's status batch … Both must produce
> the same status from the same bytes, or the two writers flap against each other
> through the shared cache entry.

The same reasoning applies to requests, but there is no staleness guard on that
leg — no timestamp or generation counter — so an older read can overwrite a newer
resolution. Basic exploration only; the exact re-seeding caller on the
navigate-back path was not traced.

Related: memory records a plan
(`2026-09-07-001-feat-transcript-interaction-records-plan.md`) to make questions,
permissions, and todos persisted transcript parts instead of transient tables,
which would remove this class outright.

## D16 — Composer images persist into other threads and new threads

Owner: prompt draft scoping, `composer/ui/submit-prompt-scope.ts:21`.

Images are not a separate store — `imageAttachments` is a memo over the draft
(`composer/composer.tsx:304`):

```ts
const imageAttachments = createMemo(() =>
  prompt.current().filter((part): part is ImageAttachmentPart => part.type === "image"),
)
```

So an attached image is a `type: "image"` part inside the prompt draft, and
clearing the draft should clear it. `createSubmitDraftLifecycle.clear()`
(`submit-draft-lifecycle.ts:28`) resets each submitted scope.

The scope is the suspect:

```ts
export function promptViewScope(input: { directory?: string; sessionId?: string; draftId?: string }) {
  return { dir: input.directory ?? "", id: input.sessionId, ...(input.draftId ? { draftId: input.draftId } : {}) }
}
```

For a **new thread** there is no session id and no draft id, so the scope collapses
to `{ dir, id: undefined }` — a single draft shared by every new thread in that
directory. An image attached in one new thread is therefore the same draft every
later new thread in that directory mounts. That accounts for the "new thread"
half of the report directly.

The "come back to another existing thread" half is not explained by that alone,
since a real session id gives a distinct scope. Not traced further — basic
exploration only. The thing to check next is whether `add()`
(`composer/ui/attachments.ts:60-68`) writes through `prompt.set(...)` with no
scope argument, and therefore lands on whichever scope is mounted at paste time
rather than the one the user believes they are typing into.

## D17 — A late-landing abort stops the wrong turn

Owner: `createPromptAbort`, `composer/ui/submit-abort.ts`, and the abort contract
it calls.

The abort carries no turn or message identifier:

```ts
abort(input: { sessionID: string; directory: string }): Promise<…>
```

`createPromptAbort` awaits that network call. Nothing scopes it to the turn the
user was looking at when they pressed send, so whatever turn is running in that
session when the request arrives is the turn that dies.

Combined with D10, the reported sequence follows: the first Enter aborts turn 1
over the network; the user sends again and turn 2 starts; the in-flight abort
lands afterwards and stops turn 2. The user observes a second stop several
seconds after the first, on a turn they never asked to cancel.

The user reports roughly five seconds. That does **not** match the optimistic
status ladder — those stages are 8s / 20s / 45s / 5min
(`store/session-status-dispatcher.ts:13-16`) — so the delay is the abort round
trip, not a client timer. Timing not measured.

Note also that `registerPendingPrompt` (`submit/pending.ts:17`) is keyed by
session id alone and overwrites any existing entry without aborting it, so a
superseded controller is dropped rather than cancelled.

Basic exploration only; not reproduced.

## D18 — An interrupted turn loses its fold control entirely

Owner: `canFoldSettled`, `message-timeline.data.ts:200`.

settled, user expanded -> [ UserMessage, TurnFold(folded=false), Part(work), Part(context) ]

This is the reported "I expanded Working, started a new turn, now no option to

The user's explicit choice also persists in `turnFoldCache`

## D19 — Session switching shifts content

Directly violates the standing requirement at the top of this document. Two
distinct symptoms reported:

**Title flickers loader → no loader → loader.** The title resolves through more

**The fold is applied after the switch, not before the first paint.** Owner:

Whether a turn folds depends on `settled`, `interrupted`, `error`, and
`foldableCount`, all derived from message data that arrives after mount. The
first frame therefore renders with the pre-hydration answer and re-folds once the
data lands, collapsing rows underneath the user.

`message-timeline.tsx:680` shows the cold/warm split feeding the same problem:

```ts

```

A session without cached measurements mounts in a deliberately degraded state and

## D20 — Fast scrolling shows blank regions that fill in as they are reached

Owner: the `rangeExtractor` override in `message-timeline.tsx:758-768`.

`message-timeline.tsx:748` sets `overscan: 50`, but the custom `rangeExtractor`
immediately below replaces it with `renderOverscan()`, which is **1** on a cold
mount and **6** once measurements exist (`:680`, `:688`). The effective band is
1–6 rows, not 50, so the `overscan: 50` option is dead and misleading.

With rows as tall and variable as transcript turns, a fast flick outruns a
six-row band: the viewport reaches rows that have not been rendered yet, which is
the reported blank area that fills in as you arrive.

`timeline-virtualization.ts:118-129` documents this exact failure mode as already
addressed — `content-visibility: auto` was removed because "a fast flick scrolls

m0164.text:
24 entries. Both recorded.

**D23 — bare "Running" / "Ran".** Found the exact line. In the `bash` renderer the command sits behind a two-part guard:

```tsx
<TextShimmer text={pending() ? "Running" : "Ran"} active={pending()} />
<Show when={!pending() && displayCommand()}>
  <ShellSubmessage text={displayCommand()} … />
</Show>
```

Two separate ways to get a bare verb:

- **While pending** — the guard literally starts with `!pending()`, so *every* running shell row shows the word "Running" and nothing else, by construction. The command only appears once the call finishes.
- **When `displayCommand()` is empty** — it's `String(props.input.command ?? props.metadata.command ?? "")`, which is `""` when neither key exists, and `""` is falsy so the `Show` renders nothing. That's reachable whenever the tool input never finished streaming: input arrives via `input_json_delta` accumulation and is only committed once the partial JSON parses. **D10 and D17 produce exactly that** — turns aborted while a tool call was mid-input. So your "sometimes" likely correlates with the aborts you've been hitting.

There's a comment directly above that guard reading *"the verb alone ('Ran') says nothing"* — the author reached the same conclusion, and the guard it annotates still permits that exact state.

**D24 — expanded card survives the fold.** Likely this exemption in `shouldFold`:

```ts
// Running-only phase fold keeps the last (live) group visible.
if (canFoldRunning && !canFoldSettled && itemIndex === lastFoldableIndex) return false
```

While a turn is running, the last group is deliberately kept out of the fold so active work stays visible — but the `TurnFold` row still renders `folded=true`. So the turn *reads* as folded while one group stays on screen under it. Each half behaves as written; together they look broken. Per-tool open state is also separately persistent (`toolOpen`, cached per session), so an expanded card stays expanded across folds and pane remounts rather than collapsing with its turn.

One caveat I recorded rather than glossed: if the turn had already **settled** when you saw this, `canFoldRunning` is false and that exemption can't apply — which would mean a different cause. Worth noting whether the turn was still running next time you hit it.

## D25 — "Thinking…" appears, drops, and returns on send

Owner: `nextThinkingVisibilityHold`,
`packages/claxedo-app/src/features/session/ui/thinking-visibility-hold.ts`.

The flap is already known and already mitigated — the module header says so:

> Status can blip idle→busy (or settled→unsettled) for a few frames while a
> stream is still running. Dropping the row immediately collapses the
> virtualizer and jumps the composer.

The mitigation is a hide-only hysteresis of **80 ms**:

```ts
export const THINKING_HIDE_HOLD_MS = 80
```

80 ms is about five frames. It covers a few-frame blip and nothing longer. On
send, the sequence is optimistic-busy → server-reported-not-yet-busy →
actually-busy, and the middle leg is a network round trip, which is one to two
orders of magnitude longer than the hold. The row therefore drops and returns —
the reported behavior — because the hold was sized for a render blip, not for a
request.

Two further observations:

- The hold is one-sided. It delays hiding but not showing, so an optimistic show
  followed by a real hide still produces a visible appear/disappear pair.
- A second, unrelated hold exists for the same family of transitions:
  `createTimelineWorkingStatus` (`timeline-working-status.ts`) defaults to
  `hideDelay = 260`. Two different constants (80 and 260) govern the visibility
  of two rows that flip on the same status changes, so they cannot stay in sync
  by construction.

Read.

## D26 — `TextShimmer` repaints text every frame, per instance, forever

Owner: `packages/ui/src/components/text-shimmer.css` and
`packages/ui/src/components/text-shimmer.tsx`.

The effect animates `background-position` on an element using
`background-clip: text`:

```css
[data-component="text-shimmer"] .ui-text-shimmer-char-shimmer[data-run="true"] {
  animation-name: text-shimmer-sweep;
  animation-duration: var(--text-shimmer-duration);   /* 1200ms */
  animation-iteration-count: infinite;
  will-change: background-position;
}

@keyframes text-shimmer-sweep {
  0%   { background-position: 100% 0, 0 0; }
  100% { background-position:   0% 0, 0 0; }
}
```

Why this is the expensive shape:

- `background-position` is not a compositor-animatable property. Combined with
  `background-clip: text` the browser must re-rasterize the glyph mask against
  the gradient **on every frame**. `will-change` promotes a layer but cannot
  remove the repaint; it only hints.
- `--text-shimmer-size: 360%` makes the gradient 3.6× the element width, so each
  of those repaints covers a large raster area.
- `animation-iteration-count: infinite` — it never stops while the row is
  mounted.
- The cost is per instance and they run concurrently. `TextShimmer` is used by
  the thinking row, every `BasicTool` title (`message-part.tsx:1232`), the bash
  verb (`:2604`), the skill title (`:3157`), and the reasoning title (`:2142`).
  Every running tool row is an independent infinite text repaint.
- The component renders the text **twice** in the DOM (`text-shimmer-char-base`
  plus `text-shimmer-char-shimmer`) for every instance, active or not, doubling
  glyph count across a long transcript.
- `data-run` only clears 220 ms after `active` goes false, so the animation keeps
  running past the point it is visible.

Performant alternatives, cheapest first:

1. **Opacity pulse** — compositor-only, no repaint. Loses the sweep look.
2. **Transform-animated overlay** — keep the gradient in a pseudo-element and
   animate `transform: translateX()` instead of `background-position`, with the
   text as a `mask-image`. Transform and opacity are the only two properties the
   compositor animates without paint.
3. **Shimmer one row at a time** — restrict the effect to the single active row
   rather than every pending tool title. Reduces N concurrent animations to 1
   regardless of which technique is used.

The `prefers-reduced-motion` branch already disables the animation entirely, so a
non-animated fallback path exists and is known to render acceptably.

Read. Not profiled — the analysis is from the animated property and the usage
count, not from a measurement. A trace should confirm paint cost before choosing
between the alternatives.

# Design requests (not defects)

Recorded separately from D1–D26: these describe intended product behavior that
differs from what is built, not code failing its own contract.

## R1 — The question tool should be its own surface, and an answered question should persist as a card

Requested by the user on 2026-09-09:

> question tool should be a clearly separate tool in UI, and the answered thing
> should be clearly visible as a very nice looking card with the answered answer,
> and not just go away like any other tool call.

### What it does today

Owner: the `question` entry in `ToolRegistry`,
`packages/session-ui/src/components/message-part.tsx:3101-3147`.

An answered question renders through the *same* `BasicTool` chrome as `bash`,
`read`, and `grep` — leading icon, title, subtitle, collapsible body:

```tsx
<BasicTool
  {...props}
  defaultOpen={completed()}
  icon="bubble-5"
  trigger={{ title: i18n.t("ui.tool.questions"), subtitle: subtitle() }}
>
```

The content is there and it does default to open once answered, so the answer is
not lost. What is missing is any visual distinction: it is a tool row among tool
rows.

Its full lifecycle today is three different surfaces:

1. **Pending** — excluded from the transcript entirely.
   `message-timeline.data.ts` `renderablePart()`:
   `if (part.tool === "question") return part.state.status !== "pending" && part.state.status !== "running"`.
   It lives in `session-question-dock.tsx` instead.
2. **Answered** — becomes an ordinary `BasicTool` row in the transcript.
3. **Turn settles** — and it disappears.

### Why it "goes away"

Step 3 is the substantive half of the request, and it is mechanical.
`isGroupFoldable` (`message-timeline.data.ts:171`) returns true for any
`group.type === "part"` whose part is a tool. An answered question *is* a tool
part, so it is foldable, it counts toward `foldableCount`, and once the turn
settles with two or more foldable groups it is hidden behind "Worked for Xs"
along with the shell commands.

So the answer the user gave — the one piece of the turn they authored themselves
— is collapsed by the same rule that collapses `ls`. That is the behavior being
objected to, and it is D4's mechanism reaching a part that should have been
exempt.

### Change points

- **Exempt questions from the fold.** `isGroupFoldable` should return false for
  `question` parts, the same way the code already special-cases them in
  `renderablePart`. This is the smallest change and it alone fixes "goes away".
- **Give it its own renderer.** Today it reuses `BasicTool`. A dedicated card —
  like `SubagentTaskCard` (`:2537`) or `ToolErrorCard`, both of which already
  escape the standard row chrome — would make it visually distinct without
  inventing a new mechanism.
- **Decide the pending surface.** The dock/transcript split means a question is
  in one place while unanswered and another once answered. If the card is to be
  the durable record, it may want to own both states rather than hand off.
- Related: `2026-09-07-001-feat-transcript-interaction-records-plan.md` already
  proposes making questions, permissions, and todos persisted transcript parts
  instead of transient dock tables. That plan is the natural home for this.

Worth noting the code already knows questions are special — `renderablePart` special-cases them (`if (part.tool === "question") return status !== "pending" && status !== "running"`) to keep pending ones out of the transcript so the dock can own them. - **Decide the pending surface** — if the card is meant to be the durable record, it may want to own the unanswered state too rather than handing off from the dock.

## D28 — Any non-zero exit code is recorded as a tool error

Owners: the per-harness adapters in `packages/agent-event-runtime/src/harnesses/`.

Every harness treats a non-zero process exit as a failure and emits `tool-error`:

**Codex** (`codex/adapter.ts:534-549`):

```ts
const exitCode = asFiniteNumber(input.row.exitCode) ?? 0
…
exitCode === 0
  ? { /* normal completion */ }
  : { type: "tool-error", toolCallId: input.toolCallId,
      error: output || `Process exited with code ${exitCode}`, … }
```

The same mapping again at `codex/adapter.ts:749-750`.

**Cursor** (`cursor/adapter.ts:356-357`):

```ts
const exitCode = asFiniteNumber(nested?.exitCode)
return exitCode !== undefined && exitCode !== 0
```

**Claude** keys off the SDK's own flag rather than the code —
`isError: block.is_error === true` (`claude/adapter.ts:220`), consumed at `:826` —
but Claude Code sets `is_error` for a non-zero Bash exit, so the observable
behavior matches.

A non-zero exit is not a failure in general; it is how a large class of standard
tools reports a normal negative result:

| Command | Exit | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `grep pattern file` | 1 | no match — expected, often the point of the call |
| `diff a b` | 1 | files differ |
| `git diff --quiet` | 1 | there are changes — this is the documented use |
| `test` / `[ … ]` | 1 | condition false |
| a failing test suite | non-zero | a real result the agent asked for |

So a `grep` that finds nothing renders identically to a crash. The transcript
loses the distinction between "the tool failed" and "the tool answered no", which
is the distinction the reader actually needs.

This compounds D22: the error card is visually heavy, and this defect makes it
fire on routine negative results, so the loudest surface in the transcript is
attached to the most ordinary outcome.

Worth noting the harnesses disagree in shape even while agreeing in effect —
Codex reads `exitCode` directly, Cursor reads a nested `exitCode`, Claude reads
`is_error`. Any fix has to land in all three or the surfaces drift.

Good news first: **the output is not truncated in the data.** A search of the

So everything needed is already client-side. What withholds it is a stack of

| # | Limit | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| D27 | `pending()` blocks clicks, hides the chevron | cannot open a running tool at all |
| D23 | command hidden while pending | cannot tell which tool it is |

describes.

## D31 — Only `http(s)` URLs are ever linkified; `file://` is inert everywhere

**Reported by the user:**

> why this link is not clickable in session that opens in sidebar

**Impact:** A path the agent hands the user cannot be acted on. They are told
where something is and then have to retype it somewhere else to reach it.

Two independent linkifiers both hardcode the scheme, so no non-`http(s)` URL is
ever clickable anywhere in the transcript.

**Markdown code spans** — `markdown.tsx:158-168`:

```js
const urlPattern = /^https?:\/\/[^\s<>()`"']+$/

function codeUrl(text: string): string | undefined {
  const href = text.trim().replace(/[),.;!?]+$/, "")
  if (!urlPattern.test(href)) return undefined
  …
}
```

`codeUrl` is what promotes a URL inside a code span to an anchor (`:596-613`).
A `file://` URL fails `urlPattern.test()`, returns `undefined`, and the link is
never created — the text renders inert.

**Tool output / message text** — `message-part.tsx:613`:

```js
[...text.matchAll(/https?:\/\/[^\s<>"'`)\]]+/g)]
```

Same restriction, independently written, in a different package.

Both patterns are also anchored to schemes only. `file://`, `vscode://`,
`claxedo://` (which this app defines for documents — see
`mcp__claxedo__documents_open`) and any custom scheme are all equally invisible.

**A second layer exists underneath.** Even if the anchor were created, a renderer
running on an `http://` origin will refuse to navigate to `file://` — that is a
browser/Electron security rule, not an app bug. So making these clickable is not

Added as **D31** — and confirmed decisively. Two independently-written linkifiers, both hardcoded to `http(s)`:

```js
// markdown.tsx:158 — code spans
const urlPattern = /^https?:\/\/[^\s<>()`"']+$/

// message-part.tsx:613 — tool output / message text
[...text.matchAll(/https?:\/\/[^\s<>"'`)\]]+/g)]
```

`codeUrl()` is what promotes a URL in a code span to an anchor. A `file://` URL fails `urlPattern.test()`, returns `undefined`, and the link is simply never created. Same restriction, separately written, in a different package. So `file://`, `vscode://`, and even your own `claxedo://` document scheme are all equally inert.

Neither pattern carries a comment explaining the restriction, and they're clearly not derived from a shared rule — so whether `https?`-only is a security decision or just an accident of whichever case each author had in mind isn't recorded anywhere.

**But widening the regex wouldn't fix it.** There's a second layer: a renderer on an `http://` origin will refuse to navigate to `file://` regardless — that's a browser/Electron security rule, not your bug. Making these clickable means routing through the existing OS-open path, `platform.openLink(url)`, rather than emitting a plain anchor. Which is very likely the same missing piece as D30, where an ordinary `http` localhost URL also wasn't clickable — pointing at click *routing* rather than pattern matching.
